seen_animation: A line-drawn crab faces the viewer, standing still between grey wavy scenery lines. It has a rounded hexagonal body, two raised claws, four short legs and two short eye stalks with diamond-shaped eyes. In frames 1-7 the crab holds still with only small shifts in the claws and eye stalks. In frame 8 both eye stalks tip outward and the eyes become small squares lower on the stalks; in frame 9 the stalks lie further outward toward the claws, near the top of the body. In frame 10 the stalks are rising back, and from frame 11 to 16 the eyes stand upright again as in frame 1, with the crab otherwise still.
seen_film: A pale ghost crab sits facing the camera on sand, slightly left of centre, with its large white claws held low in front and legs spread to both sides. Frames 1-7 it is nearly motionless with its two eye stalks upright. In frame 8 the eye stalks fold down and outward, in frame 9 they lie almost flat against the front of the carapace, in frame 10 they are blurred as they come back up, and from frame 11 to 16 they are upright again and the crab stays still.
evidence: Judged from still frames only, not playback. The one event in the film, the eye stalks folding down and coming back up, is in the same frames in the animation: upright 1-7 in both, folding at 8 in both, most folded at 9 in both, returning at 10 in both, upright 11-16 in both. The crab's body stays in one place in both, roughly centre-left of the frame. The claws, body outline with the open shoulder gap on the left, and four short legs in every animation frame match c.png. No frame shows doubled lines or a body jump; the change from frame 7 to 8 is abrupt, but the film's change from 7 to 8 is equally abrupt.
primary_gap: At the fold (frames 8-9) the animated eye stalks only tilt outward about 45 degrees and stay up near the claw arms, while in the film they lie almost flat across the top front of the body.
closes_when: In frame 9 both eye stalks lie close to horizontal along the top edge of the body, with the eyes resting at the body outline, and frame 10 shows them only partway up.
protect: Keep the timing of the fold exactly on frames 8-10 with upright eyes elsewhere; keep the crab stationary at its current place in frame; keep the doodle's claws, open left shoulder gap, flat-bottomed body and four short straight legs unchanged; keep the eye stalks as single straight strokes in the doodle's line weight.
identity_gap: The doodle in c.png has no eye stalks, so the added stalks with small diamond eyes are an addition, though they are drawn in the same plain straight-stroke style and do not change the rest of the drawing.
